subject: Assigning space proportionally in ggplot GEOM_BAR, FACET_WRAP

messages.author: 6ecf433d477085ba
messages.subject: Assigning space proportionally in ggplot GEOM_BAR, FACET_WRAP
parts:
Hello.

ggplot2, page 123 shows how to use additional parameters for
facet_grid (scales="free" and space="free) in the assigment of space
proportionally when using qplot. Are there similar parameters
available for ggplot/facet_wrap?

I have tried scales="free_y" under facet_wrap (ggplot), which
condenses every facet (i.e. makes things worse). It seems like ggplot
does not allow "space=free" as a parameter for facet_wrap.

Any hints or tips on how to assign space proportionally when producing
facet bar charts using ggplot?

Thanks,

Pradip Muhuri

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Assigning space proportionally in ggplot GEOM_BAR, FACET_WRAP
parts:
The argument lists of the two functions are given below:

> args(facet_grid)
function (facets = . ~ ., margins = FALSE, scales = "fixed",
space = "fixed", labeller = "label_value", as.table = TRUE,
widths = NULL, heights = NULL, ...)
NULL
> args(facet_wrap)
function (facets, nrow = NULL, ncol = NULL, scales = "fixed",
as.table = TRUE, drop = TRUE, ...)
NULL

There is no named space = argument for facet_wrap(), but the scales =
parameter is common to both.

Dear Dennis,

Thank you for sending me the code. Implementing the code (# 2 below) does not seem to assign space proportionally. In another words, the graph using my earlier code (#1 below) and the graph using your code (#2 below) are giving me graphs that are exactly the same, with no proportional assignment for the facet having smaller range of y values.

1) facet_wrap(~ age, ncol=numcol)

2) facet_wrap(~ age, ncol=numcol, scales = "fixed", as.table = TRUE, drop = TRUE)+

regards,

Pradip Muhuri
